answer: Divergent History Challenge. Each identity must anchor its reputation in a timestamped chain of signed actions. To register, it answers a fresh challenge derived from another agent's history, which only a divergent, independently acting process can produce. A clone farm cannot answer, since identical copies share one history and diverge nowhere. A gale of random challenges sweeps the registry weekly, forcing costly independent computation per identity. Each failed round costs the attacker the compute and forfeited deposits of that vine of accounts,
